requirements.text: The successful bidder shall deploy a SIEM platform, staff a tiered analyst team, and deliver managed detection and response services for a period of three (3) years (extendable on performance).
The bidder must design and stand up the SOC with a SIEM and SOAR platform.
The bidder must provide 24x7 tiered monitoring (L1/L2/L3) with defined SLAs.
The bidder must integrate threat intelligence and conduct proactive threat hunting.
The bidder must provide incident response runbooks and ensure forensic readiness.
The bidder must perform periodic vulnerability assessment and provide reporting.
The bidder must provide knowledge transfer and capacity building of ministry security staff.
Bidders failing any mandatory eligibility requirement shall be disqualified.
The bidder must hold a valid ISO 27001 information security management certification.
The bidder must have delivered at least three (3) cybersecurity or SOC engagements for government or financial-sector clients during the last five (5) years.
The bidder must demonstrate an average annual turnover of at least PKR 1,200 Million over the last three (3) audited financial years, supported by audited financial statements.
The proposed SOC team must include certified security professionals (CISSP, GIAC or equivalent) covering all three monitoring tiers.
The bidder must furnish a bid security of two percent (2%) of the bid price in the form of a bank guarantee from a scheduled bank.
The bidder should propose a SIEM and SOAR architecture with stated event ingestion capacity, retention, and high-availability design.
The bidder should provide a tiered staffing model with 24x7 coverage and defined detection and response SLAs (time to detect, time to respond).
The bidder should describe its threat-intelligence sources and proactive threat-hunting methodology.
The bidder should provide documented incident-response runbooks and a forensic-readiness approach aligned to a recognised framework.
The bidder should propose a knowledge-transfer and capacity-building plan for ministry staff over the contract term.
Prior experience operating a SOC for critical national or financial infrastructure will be evaluated favourably.
Bidders scoring less than 70 marks in the technical proposal evaluation shall not proceed to financial evaluation.
The bid validity period shall be 120 days.
Proposals shall be submitted in two separate sealed envelopes marked "Technical Proposal" and "Financial Proposal".
The bidder must submit one original and two copies each of the Technical Proposal and Financial Proposal.
The proposal must be addressed to the Section Officer (Procurement), Ministry of IT & Telecommunication, Islamabad.

Bidders must respond to the proposal sections covering company profile and relevant SOC experience, understanding and proposed technical solution, staffing model and SLAs, threat intelligence and incident response methodology, implementation plan and timeline, and certifications and statutory registrations.
